text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: kv-cache eviction rate spike + paging observed in us-west-2. 95th/99th generation latency increased ~3x. Alert thresholds crossed. link: https://ops.example.com/incidents/1716000001

alex: ack, I'm oncall. grabbing context and will triage.

maria: seeing massive cold misses on kv cache - eviction/sec jumped from ~220 to ~21k in last 10m. paging read ops from SSD spiked to 3.2k/s.

chris: any recent rollout to batcher or packer? could be a batching regression that inflates cache keys.

vivian: we shipped a batching change (continuous-batching heuristics) 2h ago to reduce latency on long requests. rolling config: packer.max_batch_bytes from 8MB -> 16MB and eager_prefetch enabled.

samir: that aligns. I see increased per-request KV footprints in logs: many requests now retain large KV segments.

alex: impact: A subset of customers on hosted API (tier-standard) reporting 5xxs and timeouts. Notifying support. Can we throttle prefetch and revert packer size quickly?

chris: propose immediate mitigation: 1) disable eager_prefetch, 2) set packer.max_batch_bytes back to 8MB, 3) temporary packing fairness limit for mixed workloads to prefer short requests.

vivian: I can roll a config hotfix to disable eager_prefetch and clamp packer.max_batch_bytes to 6MB (safer) across us-west-2 dedicated pool. prepping PR now.

maria: adding data: sample log snippet showing eviction surge and paging:```
[2026-04-01T14:02:03Z] eviction_rate=21045/s total_kv_entries=8.3M disk_reads=3298/s
[2026-04-01T14:02:07Z] continuous_batch_window=80ms avg_batch_size=42 packer_bytes=14.7MB
```

ops-sre: customer impact estimate: ~4% of requests elevated latency > 500ms, error rate up 0.9% region-wide. major customers A,C affected with sustained retries.

alex: Samir, can you try a targeted off-ramp: route traffic from the largest tenant on this pool to a compatible model variant (lower kv footprint) as a temporary bypass?

samir: on it. adding routing rule to divert tenant-id=acme-inc to model=redwood-lite-v2 in 2min. Will monitor.

vivian: PR merged -> rolling config change to disable eager_prefetch and set packer.max_batch_bytes=6MB. deploying to the pool.

incident-bot: Deploy started by vivian (deploy/pack-config-hotfix) — running canary on 10% of nodes.

chris: also enabling batch-scheduler fairness gate: max_concurrent_packer_per_tenant=2 and short-request-priority=true. This should prevent long requests queuing and starving short ones.

maria: after canary, eviction_rate dropped to ~1.2k/s on canary nodes, paging reads down 85% for those nodes.

vivian: canary looks good. continuing rollout to 100% across pool with 1min pause per shard.

ops-sre: monitoring: region error-rate trending down; 95th latency falling back toward baseline. still some tail spikes from mixed-shape batches.

alex: customer comms: support update sent, advising retry/backoff and noting mitigation in progress. CC engineering on followups.

samir: routing change complete for tenant acme-inc -> redwood-lite-v2. Their request error-rate normalized.

chris: post-mitigation action items: 1) revert continuous-batching heuristic tweak or add safety cap on packer bytes 2) add eviction/prefetch circuit-breaker 3) add synthetic test for mixed short/long workload fairness in canary.

vivian: creating follow-up ticket: INF-5142 "continuous-batching: safety caps + prefetch circuit-breaker". assigning to eng-runtime.

maria: for postmortem: need timeline of when heuristic rolled, metrics of kv blowup, exact customer impact windows, and a remediation checklist for faster rollback.

alex: handing to oncall SRE for follow-through. ops-sre, please take this for post-incident ops and coordinate with support for final customer report. marking incident as mitigated for now.

ops-sre: taking handoff. I'll open the incident doc, add timeline and runbook updates, and schedule a blameless postmortem. setting severity to Sev2 -> monitoring for 24h.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated: packer hotfix + routing off-ramp applied. Follow-up ticket: INF-5142. Duration: ~1h.

alex: thanks team. quick debrief on-call at 1600 UTC to assign action owners. :thumbsup:
